# Draft a Polite Complaint Email to Your Landlord About a Maintenance Issue with Qwen

> **In short:** Open Qwen, paste a short description of your maintenance issue along with your lease context, and ask it to write a polite complaint email with a clear fix-by date. You review, personalize, and send it yourself from your own account.

When your kitchen sink starts leaking or the heater dies in winter, the last thing you want is to stare at a blank email trying to find the right tone. That's exactly where Qwen helps: you describe what's wrong in plain English, and it gives you a calm, professional draft you can edit and send. By the end, you'll have a finished email in about ten minutes — without the stress of writing it from scratch.

## Before you start
- A Qwen account (free to create on the official Qwen website — see the link on this page).
- A phone or a computer with internet access.
- Your lease handy, or at least remember your unit number and the clause about repairs.
- About five to ten minutes total.

## Step 1 — Open Qwen and start a fresh chat
Go to the official Qwen website in your browser, or open the Qwen app if you already have it on your phone. Sign in with the account you created. Look for a **"New Chat"** button or a **+** icon near the top of the chat list — it usually sits on the left side of the screen. Click or tap it once. If you don't see a "New Chat" label, look for a pencil icon, a "+" symbol, or simply the empty box at the bottom of the page — that also works for starting fresh.
💬 Example: don't type anything yet — just open the empty chat first so the AI isn't influenced by an old conversation.
You'll know it worked when a blank message box appears with placeholder text like "Send a message to Qwen…" and your previous chats are out of view.

## Step 2 — Describe the maintenance problem in two or three sentences
In the empty message box, type a short, honest description of what's wrong. Don't worry about being formal — just say what happened, when it started, and how it's affecting your daily life. Then add your lease context so Qwen knows you're a tenant, not a homeowner calling about their own place. The more concrete your facts are, the more useful the email will be — vague descriptions lead to vague drafts.
💬 Example: "My kitchen sink has been leaking under the cabinet for three days. Water is pooling on the floor and the cabinet wood is starting to warp. My lease says the landlord is responsible for plumbing repairs within 48 hours. My unit is 4B and I've lived here since March 2024."
You'll know it worked when you see your full description sitting in the message box, ready to send, with the key details — date, unit, lease clause — all visible.

## Step 3 — Ask Qwen to turn it into a polite complaint email
Press the **send** button — usually an arrow icon or paper-plane shape on the right side of the message box. Then, either in the same message or as a follow-up, tell Qwen the role you want it to play, the tone, the audience, and the deadline you want in the email. The more specific you are about the shape of the email, the closer the first draft will be to what you actually need.
💬 Example: "You are a helpful writing assistant. Please turn my description above into a polite but firm complaint email to my landlord. Reference my lease clause about plumbing repairs. Ask for the issue to be fixed by Friday, June 13, 2026. Keep it under 200 words. Sign it as 'Maria Chen, Unit 4B'."
You'll know it worked when Qwen replies with a complete email — greeting, problem summary, lease reference, a clear deadline, and a signature line.

## Step 4 — Review the draft and request specific edits
Read the email Qwen wrote. Check that it sounds like you and includes the right facts. If anything feels off — too stiff, missing a detail, the wrong tone — type a follow-up request. Qwen can rewrite specific sentences, shorten paragraphs, or adjust the deadline without losing the rest of the email. If you're happy with most of it, ask for small tweaks rather than a full rewrite, so you don't lose the parts that already work.
💬 Example: "Please make the opening sentence warmer — I have a good relationship with my landlord and don't want to sound hostile. Also add one line asking for a written confirmation so I have a record."
You'll know it worked when Qwen returns a new version with your requested changes visible and the rest of the email still intact.

## Step 5 — Add your real contact details and lease specifics
The first draft will probably contain placeholders like "[your phone number]" or "[lease date]." Replace those with your actual information. Copy the email into your regular email app or a notes app, then fill in the blanks by hand. Read it out loud once — if any sentence feels robotic or stiff, rewrite that line in your own voice so the final email sounds like a real person, not a template.
💬 Example: replace "[your phone number]" with your real number, and "[lease date]" with the actual date on your signed lease, then add the landlord's email address you already have on file.
You'll know it worked when the email contains your real name, your real contact info, the correct lease date, and reads naturally when you say it out loud.

## Step 6 — Send the email from your own account
Copy the finished email into the email app you use every day — Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, or whatever is on your phone or computer. Add your landlord's actual email address, attach a clear photo of the damage if you have one, and hit send. Save a copy of the email — and a screenshot of Qwen's draft if you want — somewhere you can find later, so you have a record of what you asked for and on what date.
💬 Example: subject line — "Maintenance Request: Leaking Kitchen Sink in Unit 4B — Please Respond by June 13"
You'll know it worked when the email lands in your landlord's inbox with your name, your unit number, your lease reference, and a clear fix-by date.

## Common mistakes
- **Skipping the lease context.** Without naming the specific clause that applies, the email reads like a complaint instead of a request. Always mention the section — for example, "Section 8: Landlord Repairs" — so your landlord sees you know your rights without being aggressive.
- **Forgetting to set a specific deadline.** A polite email without a date gives the landlord no urgency and no clear next step. Always ask for a fix by a named date — give yourself at least three to five business days so the request stays reasonable.
- **Sending the Qwen draft without reading it.** Qwen usually writes well, but it can invent lease numbers, wrong unit numbers, or wrong dates if your description was vague. Read every line before you send, especially names, numbers, and dates.
- **Sending from an unfamiliar email address.** If your landlord has your old address on file and the email arrives from a new one, it sometimes gets ignored or filtered. Use the email they already have for you, not a brand-new alias.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** any time you need to write a difficult but polite message — to a noisy neighbor, a school administrator, a billing department — you can reuse this same Qwen workflow. Describe the situation, name the tone you want, ask for a deadline, and edit the draft.
- **For your business or work:** if you ever rent a workspace, studio, or office, this same approach handles repair requests, refund letters, and service complaints. The skill — describing a problem clearly and asking for a specific response — transfers everywhere.
- **If you're just getting started:** don't aim for a perfect email. Aim for a clear one: name the problem, name the lease clause, name the deadline. Polite and clear almost always beats polished and long.

## Try it now
Open Qwen right now and describe a small, low-stakes situation — a delayed package, a noisy neighbor, or a billing question. Ask it for a polite 150-word email with a specific response date. You'll have a draft you can edit and send in under five minutes, and the same workflow will feel easy when the next real maintenance issue comes up.
